notes: /stream/<token> redirects straight to the TorBox CDN once the address is warm (URL cached, file served by redirect such as MKV, link confirmed alive recently); anything else still goes through /spore-stream. A media server that relays for its client, as Jellyfin does for every Range request, saves a round trip through the proxy per request. The status stays 302; a client that inspects the Location must accept either target (see docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, shipped as a minor because any redirect-following client sees no difference)

The CDN liveness check no longer runs on the request thread for a steady play: an entry older than its two-minute window is still used for up to eight minutes more while a background probe refreshes it. A link that dies in that window is handed out until the probe returns and the next request re-resolves

The automatic .strm repair (every six hours) and the Repair broken strm files button now cover series as well as movies: an episode file with a stale address is rewritten to the current proxy URL, a file whose token Mycelium no longer knows is removed and the episode goes back on the wanted list, and a show with more than half of its files orphaned in one run is skipped and logged so a restored database cannot cascade into a library-wide delete

The Clean up duplicate strm files button says it covers movies only, which is what it always did; series duplicates are removed by the cleanup run. The repair result line now reports one set of counts per media type, including skipped files

The 1.0 compatibility promise: docs/COMPATIBILITY.md freezes the integration routes (webhooks, stream, health, metrics, setup, docs) and the environment variables by tier, with the deprecation rule, the breaking-change rule and the database guarantee; guard tests keep the document equal to the code

Upgrade and rollback: a backup runs automatically before the first start on a new version, the schema version is recorded, the startup log names both, and docs/RECOVERY.md documents the procedure with a per-release table of what each version added

Security: the Go streaming front now appends its peer to X-Forwarded-For, so the trusted-proxy header check and the login rate limiter see real addresses again; /ui/logs, the virtual-items list and the NFS/SMB tree routes are gated; the Torrentio log line and its error path no longer carry TORRENTIO_OPTS; /metrics is exempt from the login gate and enforces its own token or admin check

Module layout: app.py is split into a routes/ package of blueprints (appcore.py holds the Flask app, version.py the version), catbox.py into catbox.py, catbox_jobs.py and catbox_packs.py, the two longest play-path functions into helpers; no route, response or variable changed, guarded by a frozen route table
Docs swept against 0.17 through 0.29 with a reference guard; the dead JELLYFIN_REFRESH_DELAY_SEC setting removed; the web player works with auth disabled; the discover page number is clamped

TorBox account pool. Several TorBox API keys can be configured in Settings (section Debrid, "TorBox accounts") and are used as equal peers: a new torrent goes to the least loaded healthy account (fewest torrents, budget left, no recent 429 or auth failure), every play of a title uses the account that holds its torrent, and a disabled or failing account hands its titles over on their next play. The hourly add budget is counted per account. The Overview's TorBox card, the health rows, the Library drawer and the Prometheus gauges show accounts by label. A single-key install is unchanged: the existing key becomes account 1

Hourly TorBox id check (catbox mode): stored TorBox ids are compared with TorBox's list; an id whose torrent is gone is cleared so the next play re-adds cleanly, an item whose hash lives under another id is repointed. Nothing on TorBox is deleted; a materializing item is left alone; an empty or failing list changes nothing. The Overview's consistency card shows the last run

Overview: the TorBox card shows the idle cleanup delay again, a countdown under a minute reads "under 1 min", the activity feed only knows pills for events the backend logs, and the latency formatter is shared with the Scrapers page

A pack for another season no longer counts as a season pack for the season being searched, in every scraper, and file order mapping only applies to files with no episode tag at all. Before, a season 4 search offered season 1 and 2 packs as covering all eight episodes and could have played season 1 in order
Debridio results show the release name instead of the addon label in the swap panel and get a source label like every other scraper's

Whole-season release swap: each season in the Library drawer has a "Swap season" button listing the season packs the scrapers find, with a badge per cached pack saying which episodes it contains. Picking one moves every episode the pack contains to it (file id set up front), registers wanted episodes the pack contains, and leaves episodes the pack lacks as they are; the result lists what was swapped, registered, kept, still wanted or busy
Removed the continue-watching priority job and its CONTINUE_WATCHING_INTERVAL_MINUTES setting: it queried a per-user Jellyfin endpoint with a server key and never found anything

Jellyfin 12.0 support. Jellyfin 12 disables the legacy X-Emby-Token header, so every refresh, library lookup and health ping got a 401 while the Settings test still said ok. All requests now send the standard Authorization: MediaBrowser Token header (accepted by 10.x too), and the Settings test and health ping call the authenticated system-info endpoint so a rejected key shows as a failure

A season request registers only the episodes its cached pack actually contains. TorBox lists a cached pack's files, so episodes are matched to files at request time with their file ids stored up front (the first play skips the reconciliation); episodes the pack lacks go on the wanted list immediately with the pack excluded for them, up to three aired ones are searched right away as single episodes, unaired ones wait as not aired. Without a usable file list every episode is registered as before
The first episode of a season pack (TorBox file id 0) was re-listed on every play and failed to play when TorBox answered without a files list; a known file id of 0 is now treated as known

An episode detached from a partial season pack is searched right away and that pack is remembered as not containing the episode, so neither the monitor's search, the re-resolve of a dead release nor a re-request of the season registers the episode against it again
Registering an episode marks its wanted row found; the season pack path never did, so monitored series kept every episode "wanted" until the next monitor run

The monitor's on-disk check only looked in a "Season N" folder while the files live in "Season 0N", so for seasons 1 to 9 every registered episode was flipped back to wanted on each series check and searched again
A detached episode with a future air date returns as not aired, and its wanted row carries the series title instead of the episode's own title

The admin Library "Wanted" view now also lists titles that are in the library but still miss something: series with wanted episodes and movies on the wanted-movies list. Before, it only showed requests whose own status was wanted or upcoming, so a series that lost episodes to the season-pack repair was invisible there

Episodes of a season pack no longer play the wrong episode. When a pack did not contain an episode's file, the player silently got the largest file in the pack, usually episode 1 or 2. The first play of any episode in a pack now matches every episode of that season to a file: more naming forms are recognised, untagged files map by order only when the pack has one file per episode, and an episode the pack does not contain is detached and returns to the wanted list so the monitor searches for it on its own
Seasons already broken this way are repaired on their next play

The Overview's scraper states no longer sit on unknown. The page still never probes inline, but a stale or missing probe result now triggers a background refresh so the next poll shows the real state, the last known state is shown while that refresh runs, and the probes are warmed ten seconds after boot

The admin Overview is rebuilt as five bands, problems first. A status strip shows services, scrapers, TorBox adds, failures, the queue, titles needing attention and pending approvals, each with a link to the tab that fixes it and a glow only when something is wrong

New figures: plays today and this week (from the egress rows), pending approvals with the oldest age, titles needing attention, per-scraper state and latency, titles streamed in the last 15 minutes, and the last TorBox 429. The two TorBox cards are one card; metrics, the integration endpoints and the top folders are collapsed sections that remember their state and load only when opened

Everything the database can answer comes from one new GET /ui/api/overview call, cached 30 s, that never probes a scraper and reports which blocks failed so the page shows unavailable instead of zeros

Comet's own language and resolution Torznab attributes feed the candidate instead of a title parse alone: the resolution wins when it names one of Mycelium's buckets, and the language codes merge with what the title says. MediaFusion sends neither, so nothing changes for it

The required-rule warning looks up each scraper's capabilities in the registry instead of importing a module named after the source, which the two Torznab scrapers never had; a guard test keeps every registered scraper listed

Comet and MediaFusion as scrapers, read through their Torznab feeds by one shared adapter. Each has an enable toggle, a URL and a Test button in Settings > Scrapers; MediaFusion defaults to the public ElfHosted instance, Comet needs your own instance (the public one refuses the Torznab path). They rank between Zilean and Torrentio, share the dedupe, outage guard and latency metrics, and show on the Scrapers page
Neither feed reports cache status, so TorBox's own check decides as before. A private MediaFusion instance takes its API password; the key and any Comet access-token path are kept out of the logs

The TorBox add budget counts only uncached adds. TorBox's 60 per hour limit applies to torrents it does not have yet; cached adds fall under the general per-minute limit. Mycelium counted every add, so the TorBox adds this hour row and the Overview meter overstated usage and the client-side guard could refuse cached adds TorBox would have taken

Each add is logged with what the cache check said, corrected by TorBox's own answer; the hour count, the warning threshold and the guard cover uncached adds, the per-minute burst guard still covers every add, and both figures are shown. README corrected: the limit is per API key, not per IP

The webhook secret can be rotated from Settings. Rotate issues a new auto-generated secret and keeps the previous one valid for 24 hours, so Seerr, Radarr, Sonarr and the Jellyfin webhook plugin can be updated one by one; a webhook that still sends the old value is logged with its address and user agent

GET /ui/api/webhook-secret reports previous_valid_until during that window and POST /ui/api/webhook-secret/rotate does the rotation; both refuse when the secret comes from the WEBHOOK_SECRET environment variable

A release swap no longer waits without limit for a title that is being materialized for playback (the token lock can be held for up to ten minutes). The catbox auto-upgrader waits five seconds, then skips the title for that cycle; the admin swap waits ten seconds, then reports busy in the panel. Nothing changes on a timeout

The Overview egress tile counts MKV plays. Those plays are a redirect to the TorBox CDN, so nothing passed through Mycelium and the tile read near zero on an MKV library. The redirect branch now records the file size once per play as an estimate (a play is a redirect for a title not resolved in the last two hours); the tile shows proxied plus estimated with the split in its sub-line, and the stats payload gains egress_estimated_bytes_month
The estimate is an upper bound per play: a viewer who stops early still counts the whole file, and two viewers on one title at once count as one

Arr stubs carry the source in their name again (WEBDL-1080p, Bluray-2160p). The tag was derived from the magnet's dn= name, which the scrapers never set, so every stub was named with the bare resolution; the stored release label now feeds the detection. Titles processed before 0.21.1 keep the bare name until they are processed or swapped again
Cleanup pass over the review leftovers of 0.17 to 0.21. The title drawer is a real modal (focus moves in and back, Tab stays inside, Escape closes) and the type icons are hidden from screen readers

Settings: MultiSelect has a keyboard path, a Select whose value is not in its list shows it as a disabled entry, a secret stored in the database gets a Clear button (an environment value stays), tester messages use the schema labels

Library and Requests: an out-of-range page clamps to the last page, disabled users show in the Quotas card, approving a paused request clears the pause note, duplicate requests by one user count once, the Arr card only renders with the mirror on, the bulk bar keeps its final result line, blacklist titles load in grouped queries

Release swap: negative season or episode references are rejected on both endpoints, a swap reuses the candidate list from the last five minutes instead of scraping twice, and the catbox upgrader shares release_swap.swap
The source column means release source: the processor writes the label (WEB-DL, BluRay, REMUX) or nothing, never a scraper name, and a one-off startup migration blanks scraper names left in old rows

Pick another release from the Library drawer: the Release card (movies) and every present episode row show the candidate list the processor saw, with quality, size, seeders, languages, which scrapers returned it, whether TorBox has it cached, and the rule that dropped a candidate. Choosing one swaps the release behind the existing token, so the next play uses it and nothing on disk changes; the old release can be blacklisted in the same step

The swap clears the TorBox and RealDebrid ids and the URL and fast-start caches for the token, resets the playability record, and keeps the request row's status; a stream in progress may switch to the new file on its next range request
Whole-season swap (picking a new season pack for every episode at once) is a follow-up

The monthly request cap can be set on the Users tab: the column is an inline field (blank means no cap) that saves on Enter or when you leave it. Until now the tab only displayed the cap, so the quotas enforced since 0.20.0 could not be changed from the SPA

Admin Requests tab rebuilt on the Library kit: views Pending, Approved, Denied and All with counts; filters by user, type and date; sortable columns; server-side paging; Approve, inline Deny with a reason, and Reopen for a denied request; a Quotas card with each user's requests this month against their cap; the auto-approve rules moved under the table. Clicking a title opens the same drawer as the Library tab

Monthly request quotas are enforced: a user at the cap is refused with a clear message, an auto-approve user at the cap has new requests wait for review until the month resets, and admins are never limited. Denied requests do not count toward the cap

The title drawer gains Forget request, which drops the title from the Library table but keeps its files and its request history; a title outside the library now explains itself instead of showing a loading header
Removed GET /ui/api/requests/all, unused since the Library tab

Admin Library tab: every title in one table with status, failure reason, release, requester, playability, missing-episode and retry badges; saved views (Needs attention, Wanted, Queue, Incomplete series, Unmirrored); filters by type, status, problem, requester and date; sortable columns; server-side paging; a bulk action bar with retry, re-resolve, mirror and remove, plus run now and drop from queue in the Queue view

Title drawer with everything Mycelium knows about a title and its actions: retry, re-resolve, purge, mirror to the arr, blacklist a hash, reset playability, per-episode retry and series recheck, a per-title quality override, request history and the activity log

The admin Requests tab keeps pending approvals and the auto-approve rules; its request list moved to the Library tab. Maintenance lost its per-token playability panel, the Blacklist tab shows which titles used each hash, and the Overview's queue count links to the Queue view

Retrying a request keeps its quality, source and hash; the admin Retry and Remove routes find any request, not only the 1,000 newest; bulk retries run at most three pipelines at a time; playability is looked up through one grouped join
Migration: activity_log gains a nullable imdb_id column plus indexes on activity_log, user_requests, wanted_episodes and requests(info_hash)

The setup wizard is driven by the settings schema: eleven steps declared next to the schema, every field through the same kit as Settings (labels, help, dropdowns, pickers, Test buttons), pre-filled on a re-run. The quality step edits the real filter rules; the retired QUALITY_PREFERENCE, ALLOW_4K, PREFER_HEVC and AUDIO_LANGUAGE_PREFERENCE names are gone

New GET /setup/schema and POST /setup/picker/<name>; POST /setup/test/<kind> also accepts JSON. The setup surface is open only while nothing can log in, or to an admin; a logged-in non-admin on a never-completed install can no longer reach it

Settings rebuilt around a field schema: a section sidebar, a label and help line on every setting, real controls (toggles, dropdowns, searchable multi-select, an orderable sort order, number fields with units, password fields with reveal), a Simple/Advanced switch, dependent fields that hide until their toggle is on, and a search box
Every integration has a Test button that uses the values as typed; Radarr and Sonarr root folders and quality profiles are loaded from the arr with a Load button

New settings RADARR_QUALITY_PROFILE and SONARR_QUALITY_PROFILE (by name; blank keeps the first profile). ARR_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES and DISK_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES are editable in Settings (restart required)
OIDC settings are read through the Settings overlay (restart applies them); Save writes only the fields you changed
The setup wizard's connection tests and the old /ui/api/arr-import routes share the same testers; the arr-import routes remain as aliases for one release

The on-disk deletion check (a title whose .strm files are gone was deleted in Jellyfin) is its own hourly job, gated on CATBOX_MODE and DISK_SYNC_ENABLED instead of the Radarr/Sonarr mirror. Jellyfin-only setups without the webhook plugin now converge too; DISK_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES (60) sets the cadence
The arr reconcile counts a title whose arr is not configured (single-arr setup) as skipped instead of failed

The Radarr/Sonarr reconcile is now the source of truth for deletions: a mirrored title the arr confirms it no longer has, or whose .strm files are gone from disk, is purged instead of re-added. The delete webhooks make it instant; without them cleanup converges within ARR_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES (default 60, was six hours)

Guards refuse to purge when an arr lists nothing, when more than half the mirrored titles vanish at once, or when the media tree is empty; refused titles are re-added as before. ARR_SYNC_PURGE_ENABLED=false keeps the mirror add-only
Every reconcile purge is recorded in the activity feed with its reason
Series folder renames roll back when the path update fails, so folder and database never disagree
Health card: warns when a Jellyfin library on Mycelium's media has Trickplay or chapter-image extraction on, and shows TorBox adds used this hour (amber from 45 of 60)
Health rows now show their reason in the Overview, including why stub files are not being written
The built-in manual covers Radarr, Sonarr and Maintainerr, the Jellyfin webhook plugin and library settings, Seerr outcome reporting, and the TorBox add budget for auto-requesters such as Suggestarr

Stub files for Radarr and Sonarr (ARR_STUBS_ENABLED): a tiny fake .mkv per title in a folder the arrs scan as their root, so mirrored titles show as owned with the quality Mycelium found instead of Missing
Maintainerr's delete-files action and a manual file delete in Radarr now remove the title from Mycelium
Needs Catbox mode; single-arr setups are supported; the health card reports a missing stub folder
Setup steps in docs/INTEGRATIONS.md
A root folder picked in Settings > Radarr / Sonarr now takes effect immediately instead of after a restart
The delete webhook checks ownership locally first, so Jellyfin deletions in other libraries no longer cost a TMDB lookup
The Radarr/Sonarr reconcile job reports already-present titles separately from adds, and arr calls time out after 8 seconds
Settings > Radarr / Sonarr: Test buttons that report the arr's version, using the URL and key as typed
Root folders are now dropdowns filled from Radarr and Sonarr by a Load folders button, with free space shown
Remove from library now really tells Seerr: the title is requestable again in Seerr immediately instead of after its next availability sync
Seerr reporting finds titles by TMDB id, so it also works for titles requested before 0.14.0, for series, and for titles added from Discover that exist in Seerr
A failed request declines every open Seerr request for that title
Remove from library now tells Seerr the title is gone, so it can be requested again right away instead of after Seerr's next sync
Delete and Remove from library clear the per-user request rows that kept showing a stale badge and a greyed-out request button
The Delete confirmation explains that the title stays in Jellyfin and points at Remove from library
The first Jellyfin refresh after a host reboot is no longer skipped
Docs: Jellyfin takes about a minute to show a reported change; that is its library monitor delay, not a missing scan
Radarr and Sonarr can mirror Mycelium's library as monitored, search-off entries, so Seerr, Maintainerr and calendar widgets see your titles (ARR_SYNC_ENABLED, off by default)
A new /webhook/arr endpoint purges a title when Radarr, Sonarr or Jellyfin reports it deleted, so deletions made elsewhere no longer leave rows behind
Jellyfin is told exactly which files changed instead of being asked for a full library scan after every add and purge
Seerr is told the outcome: added titles show Available at once, failed ones are declined so requests stop showing Processing forever
See docs/INTEGRATIONS.md for the setup steps
Size caps can now be set per resolution, so you can allow large 4K files while keeping 1080p modest
A new setting chooses whether the smallest or largest file wins when everything else is equal
The README screenshot shows the current interface again
The setup wizard now creates your first admin account, so an install with authentication enabled can no longer finish setup with no way to log into it
A new recovery guide covers what to do when Mycelium comes back with an empty library, starting with how to tell whether anything was actually lost
A failed backup restore reports the failure instead of looking identical to a successful one
The egress meter is held in place by tests, after a missing exemption made it silently report nothing
The native hash index now fetches only the pages added since the last sync instead of downloading the full 1.45 GB snapshot four times a day
The watchdog now alerts when the database is empty but .strm files still exist on disk, the signature of a database pointed at the wrong volume
Monthly proxied egress is shown on the admin Overview, so you can see how close you are to your TorBox plan's bandwidth floor
Resolved CDN links expire inside TorBox's three hour window instead of after twenty-three, so a cached link is never dead on arrival
A fresh install with authentication enabled can reach its setup wizard, and the setup endpoints refuse anonymous writes once setup is complete
The running version is shown in the footer, so you can tell which build you are on at a glance
The Releases tab announces the current version again: this file had silently fallen six releases behind
A hand-supplied Debridio config token can no longer send your TorBox key: the key is stripped by value, under any field name and either base64 encoding
Native-mode Zilean works again: the built-in index has no URL, but the health gate demanded one, so it was skipped for every search and shown as down
The admin Scrapers page lists every scraper, including disabled and down ones, instead of hiding them
/login sends you to the app when authentication is disabled, instead of a login page with no way to log in
A rate-limited TorBox CDN no longer produces fake tiny streams or truncated responses: streams that cannot start now answer with a proper retryable error
Mid-stream CDN drops resume from the exact byte where the transfer died
The Jinja dashboard is gone: the React UI is the only interface, so features are built once instead of twice
New Playability panel in admin Maintenance, with a Re-resolve button that previously required curl
Debridio is queried as a plain scraper: your TorBox key is no longer sent to it
Preferences saved by the shared-password login persist instead of silently reverting
Streaming moves to a Go front process: each open stream costs a goroutine instead of a worker thread, removing the ceiling on simultaneous streams
The admin System health card shows which process is serving streams
The React UI is now the default
The serving thread pool grows from 16 to 64, configurable with GUNICORN_THREADS
The TorBox rate-limit budget is enforced through the database, so it holds across restarts and processes
The frontend is code-split: the first page load drops from 949KB to 27KB
Stats, indexes and repair jobs reworked for large libraries
The Library pages movies server-side: libraries over 10,000 titles were silently showing only the newest 10,000
Cleanup runs finish dramatically faster: it no longer pauses two seconds after every healthy file
RealDebrid on-play waits are capped at 45 seconds like the TorBox path
The admin Overview has a working TorBox Usage card again: torrent count, total size, your plan, and a breakdown by download state
Toast notifications are back: bottom-corner confirmations when you add, request, sync or delete, and live activity toasts in the admin
The sidebar and login page show the logo mark next to the wordmark again
The region picker actually saves now, for both the shared-password and per-user logins, and the default region is United States
The admin Overview shows all four integration endpoints again (Seerr webhook, TorBox push, stream prefix, webhook secret), each with a Copy button
Releases is its own admin tab
The Library series list is searchable, like movies
The Movies / Episodes / Series / Wanted tiles return to the admin Overview
Fix: the Discover page rendered for a moment and then went black. The new trending hero and the trending row shared one cached query under different shapes, so the row tried to list an object
A wrong shape now shows the empty state instead of blanking the page
The whole web UI is redesigned: new dark palette, self-hosted fonts, SVG icons, a sidebar with live counts and a TorBox status pill

Every screen relaid out: Discover gains a trending hero, Library gets stat tiles and a table view, Watchlist shows Trakt and MDBList sync cards, Search becomes result rows with facets, Requests shows your monthly quota, Wanted shows both backlogs with retry-all
The admin is now fully native: nine tabs replacing the old embedded dashboard, including a chip-based filter rules editor, live scraper health, and a structured log viewer

New: set UI_V2=true to also serve the redesigned login, setup wizard and admin at their own URLs; without it those three pages look exactly as before. The old pages stay reachable at /login/classic, /setup/classic and /admin/classic either way
Fix: quality and language choices made in the setup wizard now actually apply (they were silently ignored since the filter-rules model landed)
Fix: the admin dashboard reloaded itself every two minutes, throwing away your scroll position, the open tab and anything half-typed
The repair history on the Maintenance tab now refreshes in place on the same schedule, so nothing gets staler
Your search text in the repair table now survives a refresh instead of silently ceasing to filter

Fix: the NFO title repair never repaired anything - an ElementTree element's truth value is its child count, so the guard skipped every file and the button silently did nothing in every version that had it
The repair now covers movies as well as series, rewriting a movie as a movie document keeping its year rather than as a tvshow
The Maintenance button is now called 'Fix library titles'
If you are on 0.7.5 or earlier, that button did nothing; run it again after upgrading
Fix: the retry queue never drained - a scheduling collision re-queued a title every 60 seconds forever, bypassing the give-up cap, and nothing enforced one row per title or pruned old rows
Upgrading collapses any duplicate rows you already have, keeping the furthest-along attempt; one row per title is enforced from then on
Rows still queued after a week are now pruned twice daily
New: a 'Clear retry queue' button in Maintenance, since the dashboard showed the queue but gave you no way to empty it

Fix: Mycelium imported your whole TorBox account on a timer and at every boot, creating library entries with no request behind them that nothing in the UI could list or remove; importing is now only what the button does
Fix: every series showed as 'Season 01' in Jellyfin, because tvshow.nfo took its title from the season folder instead of the show folder
Fix: the retired filter settings were still editable in the admin UI, so toggling EXCLUDE_CAM or PREFER_HEVC saved a value nothing reads
New: a 'Fix series titles' button in Maintenance, which repairs tvshow.nfo files written by earlier versions
After upgrading: run Fix series titles, then Import TorBox library to adopt any orphaned auto-imports, then a Jellyfin scan

Fix: 'Remove from library' left the title visible in Jellyfin - the .strm files were deleted but the artwork and tvshow.nfo beside them were not, so the folder never emptied and Jellyfin kept scanning a valid-looking show
The purge only removes filenames Mycelium writes, and skips any folder still holding a .strm, so a sibling title's files and anything you put there yourself are left alone
Fix: a purge could delete the files and never tell Jellyfin, because the 60s refresh debounce swallowed the scan; a purge now forces it
Fix: spore-nfs and spore-smb logged a tree refresh every ten seconds each - about 17,000 lines a day - which rotated real history out of the log; they now log only on a change
Note: a title purged by an earlier version already left its artwork behind. Those folders hold no .strm and can be deleted directly.
New: PUID/PGID support, the same variables Jellyfin and Plex use - set them to your Jellyfin user and Mycelium stops writing files your media server cannot delete

The ownership pass runs once, re-runs if you change the ids, and is skipped on normal restarts; a failed pass is not recorded as done, so it retries rather than booting into a database it cannot write
PUID=0 is the default and changes nothing, so existing deployments are unaffected until they opt in
Fix: the SMB share keeps port 445 under a non-zero PUID, which would otherwise have stopped binding silently
Fix: a spore-nfs or spore-smb process that dies is now logged; previously the share just vanished with nothing in the log

Fix: deleting a request now actually deletes it - the webhook dedup key, the queued retry and (with the new button) the .strm files went with it, where before they survived and broke the next request for the same title
Fix: re-requesting something you deleted was answered 'duplicate' and silently never processed, for up to 24 hours

Fix: a re-requested series was marked failed while its episodes were sitting in the library, because 'already registered' and 'could not register' were the same return value; a genuine write failure is still reported as a failure
Fix: a deleted request could reappear an hour later when its queued retry fired
New: a second 'Remove from library' button beside Delete, which also deletes the .strm files so the title leaves Jellyfin and Plex; Delete keeps its old meaning of forgetting the record only
Release filtering is now a four-state rule model: twelve booleans retired in favour of 37 settings across seven categories, each value marked preferred, excluded, required or included
Evaluation is order-independent: every category votes against the full candidate pool and the votes are unioned, so the result no longer depends on the order rules happen to be written in
Soft relaxation is assessed globally, so two categories that each drop a different half of the pool no longer empty it between them
Every rejected candidate now carries the rule and value that dropped it, and whether that rule then relaxed
The settings page renders seven category panels with per-value chips instead of 35 comma-separated text boxes; each category's vocabulary is a dropdown, so an invalid value cannot be typed
A value stored from .env that is not in its vocabulary is shown struck through with an explanation, where before it warned once at startup and was then invisible while matching nothing
SORT_ORDER is configurable across ten criteria; the default reproduces the previous ranking exactly

Behaviour change: EXCLUDE_LANGUAGES loses an undocumented rescue, and Dolby Vision detection now catches a trailing .DV the old pattern missed, so EXCLUDE_DV_P5 drops some releases that previously passed
Naming fix: QUALITY_PREFERENCE held a RESOLUTION despite its name; it becomes RESOLUTION_PREFERRED
Retired settings migrate once at startup, guarded by FILTER_RULES_MIGRATED so a restart cannot overwrite later edits, and any retired key left in .env is named in a startup warning
Fix: the OIDC toggle in the admin UI now takes effect, in both directions

Fix: Debridio results were systematically outranked on language - Debridio ships language data as flag emoji in the stream title and Mycelium was discarding all of it, so every Debridio result scored worst-but-one on the third ranking term and lost to any Torrentio release that spelled out ENGLISH
Fix: language detection now lives in one place and is used by all three scrapers, reading flag emoji as well as release-name tokens
Note: better data can move a release DOWN as well as up - a release flagged only French and German now correctly ranks below a preferred-language release, where it previously scored as unknown
Fix: the detectable vocabulary grows from 4 language codes to 34, and AUDIO_LANGUAGE_PREFERENCE / EXCLUDE_LANGUAGES are now validated on save instead of silently accepting a code that never matches
Fix: Zilean's total absence of language data is now explicit rather than indistinguishable from a release that simply did not state its language

Added: Debridio joins Zilean and Torrentio as a third scraper, queried first when enabled. Needs DEBRIDIO_API_KEY (your Debridio account key) and reuses your existing TORBOX_API_KEY as the provider key; with either missing it stays out of rotation entirely

Added: the Debridio config is deliberately permissive rather than mirroring Mycelium's filters down into it - ours are soft and self-disabling, Debridio's are hard, so pushing them down would delete streams the ranker would have chosen to allow
Added: a source_unique_win metric counting only wins where no other scraper returned that hash, since plain win rate overstates whichever scraper sits first in the priority order

Fixed: candidate discovery is one scrapers.fetch_candidates() orchestrator instead of nine hand-rolled call sites in three different patterns; all scrapers are queried concurrently and merged in priority order, so duplicate hashes resolve deterministically instead of by race
Fixed: a transient scraper outage could delete the library - cleanup read a total upstream outage as 'this title no longer exists' and unlinked the .strm, its .nfo and the database row
Fixed: a lapsed Debridio subscription reported itself healthy, because both health probes treated any status below 500 as up and Debridio is the only scraper that authenticates
Fixed: with LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG, urllib3 logged Debridio's full request path - including the base64 config segment holding both API keys - into the admin Logs tab
Fixed: the web player never saw Debridio; it now shares the orchestrator's fetch and applies its own browser-compatibility scoring to the result
Fixed: Catbox cached the outage sentinel for 6 hours instead of not caching it, so a title went un-searched long after an outage ended

Fix: catch-up requests were recorded under their raw IMDB id (tt2017109 instead of the real title), which then carried into the library folder name on disk - Seerr's request API has no title field, so the fallback fired every time
Fix: titles now resolve through TMDB, the same fallback the webhook parser uses when a payload arrives without a subject
Repair: existing tt-named requests and folders can be fixed with the 'Fix IMDB titles' button in Admin > Maintenance
Internal: strm_generator's test mocks are no longer dependent on test import order, which had been silently running several tests against the real settings/db modules

Fix: Seerr/Jellyseerr requests intermittently failed with '400 No IMDB id found', most often for TV and anime - the TMDB fallback that resolves tmdbId to an IMDB id was only reachable through a successful Seerr API round-trip, so it was skipped whenever Seerr was unreachable, returned 404/401, or the payload carried no request_id
Fix: requires TMDB_API_KEY to be a v4 Read Access Token (starts with 'ey') - the API uses bearer auth, so a v3 key 401s silently on every call
Fix: the webhook no longer calls Seerr when SEERR_URL is unset, instead of making a guaranteed-to-fail request and logging a misleading warning every time
Fix: an unsubstituted {{media_tmdbid}} in a webhook template raised out of int() as an HTTP 500 with a traceback instead of a clean 400
Fix: the 'no IMDB id' error now names the subject, the tmdb_id tried, and whether TMDB_API_KEY is set, instead of one opaque string for four unrelated causes
Security: OIDC/trusted-proxy logins no longer implicitly become admin - a real per-user role is resolved/created instead
Security: session secret no longer signs cookies with the well-known default value if left unchanged
Security: added missing admin-only checks to ~30 previously-unprotected admin routes
Security: Web Player streaming routes now require an authenticated, enabled session (previously open once a token was known)
Security: trusted-proxy default narrowed to loopback only, webhook secret comparison is now constant-time
Security: Spore TCP server now binds to loopback by default instead of all interfaces
Fix: a transient scraper/cache error on one episode could mark an entire multi-season request failed, discarding already-added seasons
Fix: the retry queue could silently drop a failed retry and stall the rest of that cycle's batch
Fix: cleanup/repair and folder-migration could leave orphaned database rows behind, permanently blocking recreation of a title
Fix: folder rename/merge could corrupt a sibling folder's database paths when one folder name was a prefix of another
Fix: Plex fast-start MP4 cache could corrupt sample offsets for CDN files with a second data block after the moov atom
Fix: HTTP suffix byte-ranges (bytes=-N) were parsed as the first N bytes instead of the last N
Fix: CSRF protection was effectively disabled on ~27 internal API routes
